title: Two's company: why Switzerland will not let a guinea pig live alone

sents.en: Swiss law treats loneliness as a form of cruelty, at least for certain small, furry creatures.
sents.zh: 瑞士法律把孤独视为一种虐待，至少对某些毛茸茸的小动物是这样。

sents.en: Owners have had to adjust, and at least one entrepreneur has spotted a gap in the market.
sents.zh: 主人们不得不适应，而至少有一位创业者从中发现了商机。

sents.en: Switzerland has a reputation for meticulous rules, and its animal-welfare laws are among the strictest anywhere.
sents.zh: 瑞士以规定细致入微出名，它的动物福利法也是全世界最严格的之一。

sents.en: Since 2008 they have obliged owners of sociable species, guinea pigs included, to keep them with at least one of their own kind.
sents.zh: 自 2008 年起，这些法律要求群居动物（包括豚鼠）的主人，至少要让它们和一只同类住在一起。

sents.en: A solitary guinea pig, the thinking goes, is a forlorn one.
sents.zh: 人们的想法是：一只孤零零的豚鼠，就是一只可怜兮兮的豚鼠。

sents.en: The animals squeak, groom each other and huddle together for warmth; deprived of company, they can become listless and withdrawn.
sents.zh: 这些小动物会吱吱叫、互相梳理毛发、挤在一起取暖；一旦没了同伴，它们可能变得无精打采、孤僻退缩。

sents.en: The rule creates an awkward dilemma when one of a pair dies.
sents.zh: 当一对豚鼠中有一只死去时，这条规定就带来了一个尴尬的两难局面。

sents.en: Buying a replacement solves the immediate problem but starts the cycle again, since the newcomer will probably outlive its elderly companion.
sents.zh: 再买一只能解决眼前的问题，但又会让循环重新开始，因为新来的那只很可能比年老的同伴活得更久。

sents.en: Owners can end up trapped in an endless chain of guinea pigs, each new purchase prolonging the obligation by several years.
sents.zh: 主人们可能陷入一条没完没了的“豚鼠链”，每买一只新的，就让这份责任又延长好几年。

sents.en: Some resort to scouring online adverts for an elderly animal that needs a home.
sents.zh: 有人不得不在网上广告里四处搜寻，想找一只需要人收养的老年豚鼠。

sents.en: Into this niche stepped a breeder who began renting out guinea pigs.
sents.zh: 就在这个缝隙里，一位饲养者站了出来，开始出租豚鼠。

sents.en: A bereaved animal can be paired with a hired companion of a suitable age; when it eventually dies, the lodger goes back and is put up for hire again.
sents.zh: 失去伴侣的豚鼠可以配上一只年龄合适的“租来的伙伴”；等它最终离世，这位“房客”就被送回去，再次出租。

sents.en: The arrangement sounds faintly comic, yet it addresses a genuine welfare problem.
sents.zh: 这种安排听上去有点滑稽，但它确实解决了一个真实存在的动物福利问题。

sents.en: Guinea pigs are not the only beneficiaries of Swiss solicitude.
sents.zh: 享受到瑞士这份关怀的，不只有豚鼠。

sents.en: Budgerigars and other flock birds are likewise entitled to company of their own species.
sents.zh: 虎皮鹦鹉和其他群居鸟类，同样有权拥有同类的陪伴。

sents.en: In 2018 the government banned the practice of plunging live lobsters into boiling water; they must now be stunned first.
sents.zh: 2018 年，政府禁止把活龙虾直接扔进沸水；现在必须先把它们弄晕。

sents.en: For several years, new dog owners even had to sit a short course before bringing a puppy home, though that requirement has since been scrapped.
sents.zh: 有好几年，新养狗的人甚至要先上一门短期课程，才能把小狗带回家，不过这项要求后来取消了。

sents.en: Critics deride all this as the nanny state run amok.
sents.zh: 批评者嘲笑这一切是“保姆式国家”管过了头。

sents.en: Why, they ask, should bureaucrats dictate how many rodents a family keeps?
sents.zh: 他们质问：凭什么要官僚来规定一家人养几只啮齿动物？

sents.en: Defenders counter that a pet is not a toy, and that an animal cannot lodge a complaint about its own living conditions.
sents.zh: 支持者反驳说，宠物不是玩具，而且动物也没办法为自己的生活条件提出投诉。

sents.en: Most Swiss seem untroubled either way.
sents.zh: 不管怎样，大多数瑞士人似乎都不太在意。

sents.en: In a country that prizes privacy and quiet, it seems fitting that even its smallest residents are guaranteed a friend.
sents.zh: 在一个珍视隐私和安静的国家，就连最小的居民也被保证有一个朋友，这似乎也挺合适。
